$comment: Baseline allowlist for scripts/verify. Public output must stay byte-identical during the current monorepo-migration phase — any pre-existing issue found here is NOT fixed by the verifier or by this file, only documented so CI stays green today. Any NEW issue (a different check/code/route triple) still fails the build. Every entry needs a self-contained `reason` (don't reference other entries or files outside this repo). Remove an entry once the underlying issue is actually fixed — a run that never re-triggers it is reported as 'stale' by the verifier.

entries.reason: Pre-existing content data: packages/content/src/data/projects.ts has two distinct real projects in Calpe (slugs "hormigon-impreso-calpe" and "hormigon-impreso-calpe-2") whose title-building fields produce the exact same generated <title>. Public output must stay byte-identical during this migration phase, so not fixed here; belongs in a content-data task (disambiguate the title, e.g. by district).

Pre-existing content data bug in packages/content/src/data/projects.ts: the project with slug "hormigon-pulido-alicante" has `town: 'Benissa'` (a different real job there, district "Montemar la Viña" vs. the other Benissa project's "Monte Mar"), so its generated title/description collide with the actual "hormigon-pulido-benissa" project. The "-alicante" slug itself is a public URL (a WordPress-era 301 in next.config.ts targets it), so it can't just be renamed to match the town — this needs a real content-data fix (retitle using the district, not the town), done separately; not fixed here since public output must stay byte-identical during this migration phase.

apps/web/src/lib/config/nap.ts reads process.env.EMAIL_DESTINO directly (same as the pre-migration lib/config.ts), so the bare variable NAME appears as a property-access string in a client chunk — only the NAME, never the value: Next doesn't inline a non-NEXT_PUBLIC_ var into client code. Not fixed here: public output must stay byte-identical during this migration phase. Worth a later task to separate the publicly-displayed email (business.email) from the lead-form destination, and to move EMAIL_DESTINO out of ServerEnvSchema so it stops being treated as a server secret.

Intentional, by design, not a leak of a secret: apps/web/src/lib/config/nap.ts's nap.email falls back to EMAIL_DESTINO when set, and that value is what apps/web/src/components/layout/Pie.tsx's footer, /presupuesto and the legal pages render as the business contact email, and what schema.tsx puts in the LocalBusiness JSON-LD — so it's expected to appear verbatim across every prerendered page under apps/web/.next/server/app (HTML and RSC payloads alike). If EMAIL_DESTINO is set to the lead-form's real destination address in production, that same address becomes the site's publicly-displayed NAP email too — a pre-existing content-data/config conflation, not something this check can or should flag differently. Not fixed here: public output must stay byte-identical during this migration phase. Worth a later task to separate the publicly-displayed email (business.email) from the lead-form destination, and to move EMAIL_DESTINO out of ServerEnvSchema so it stops being treated as a server secret.
